$schema_note: Edit this file to register a new natural-language MCP trigger. Restart the ai-governor-harness MCP server to pick up changes — no TypeScript rebuild required. Each entry tells INVARIANT#19_MCP_TRIGGER_BYPASS: when `keywordPattern` matches in a response AND `bypassPattern` matches in the same response (indicating direct REST/CLI access), fire a violation UNLESS the tool_call_log shows `expectedMcpPrefix`. Patterns are compiled with the `i` flag.
$cross_check_with_mcp_config: If `mcp_config.json` does not register a server matching `mcpServerName`, that entry is auto-skipped at load time (logged to stderr). This prevents false positives for triggers whose backing server was uninstalled.

triggers.name: opencrab
triggers.description: OpenCrab keyword requires mcp__opencrab__ontology_query. Direct localhost:8001 REST access is a bypass — only allowed as fallback after the MCP tool itself fails.

triggers.name: langfuse
triggers.description: Langfuse session search must use the hermes-langfuse-search skill (which routes to mcp__hermes-agent__hermes_session_search) or scripts/search.py — never direct REST.

triggers.name: korean_law
triggers.description: Korean-law queries must go through mcp__korean-law__ tools (search_law / get_law_text / verify_citations). Direct law.go.kr scraping bypasses citation verification.

triggers.name: notebooklm
triggers.description: NotebookLM access must use mcp__notebooklm__ tools. The `nlm` CLI is the auth helper — direct query/chat CLI usage skips the MCP layer.
